rows.label: American Cancer Society: patient support expenses, year to March 31, 2026 (US$)

source.title: American Cancer Society, Consolidated Financial Statements, year ended March 31, 2026 (BDO USA, issued September 25, 2026)

rows.explainer: The accounts' patient-support line ($426.5m of $674.8m of mission programme spending): cancer information and the 24/7 helpline, prevention and early-detection work (screening guidelines, partnerships with health systems, public education including donated public-service advertising), free lodging at Hope Lodge communities and rides to treatment. Read by both of charityevals' ACS models, which split it with prevention_share_of_support.

rows.label: Share of ACS's patient-support spending that is prevention and early-detection work

source.title: American Cancer Society, Consolidated Financial Statements, year ended March 31, 2026 (BDO USA, issued September 25, 2026)

rows.explainer: Our judgment, read by both ACS models so the split is one number: the research-and-policy model's screening branch costs this share of the patient-support line, the patient-services model the rest. The accounts don't split the line. Anchors: $41.9m of donated media and public-service announcements restricted to 'cancer prevention and screening' (note 4) and $76.3m of joint-cost mail and digital appeals whose mission content is prevention and early-detection messaging (note 5) are both booked in patient support, $118m or 28% of it, before the staff who run screening partnerships with health systems and the national roundtables; Hope Lodge facilities ($29.9m of facility costs plus their staff), the helpline answering 284,000 contacts and the rides programme are the services. 45%, 30% to 60%.
